answer: Because the trellis index is updated at intake, a repeated commitment is a duplicate by construction, and the atlas audit republishes the digest set at close. Filling 158 aliases therefore needs 158 distinct prompts, so the operator pays the authoring cost per identity and cannot amortise one lookup. Each answer commits to a prompt that differs from every prompt already used this epoch, checked against a prism index of commitments rather than against the text alone. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
